title: Defusing 500-Pound Bombs with a Wrench
hook: One ticking clockwork fuse, zero second chances.

scenes.text: During the London Blitz, one in ten German aerial bombs failed to explode on impact, burrowing twenty feet into city streets.

scenes.text: Royal Engineer bomb disposal officers climbed down dark, muddy timber shafts to disarm 500-pound iron monsters by hand.
scenes.imagePrompt: Timber-shored underground trench pit with wooden ladder, water seepage, and the tail fin of an iron aerial bomb half-buried in clay. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Royal Engineer bomb disposal officers climbed down dark, muddy timber shafts to disarm 500-pound iron monsters by hand.

scenes.text: Many bombs were fitted with treacherous clockwork delay fuses or anti-handling booby traps designed to detonate if touched.

scenes.voicedText: Many bombs were fitted with treacherous clockwork delay fuses or anti-handling booby traps designed to detonate if touched.

scenes.text: Officers used copper wrenches and liquid nitrogen to freeze ticking clockwork timers before unscrewing the explosive gaine.

scenes.voicedText: Officers used copper wrenches and liquid nitrogen to freeze ticking clockwork timers before unscrewing the explosive gaine.

scenes.text: Once disarmed, the hollow bomb casing was paraded through neighborhoods to cheers, while its explosive was safely burned.
